 FBI investigates apparent breach of national crime database
 Saturday, 21 November 2026, 04:23 
 Photo source: CNN 
 The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center, a nationwide database used by law enforcement. 
 Two people briefed on the investigation said the FBI is examining an apparent breach of the database, which connects federal, state and local law enforcement. The intrusion is the second such breach in recent months.
 This is reported by CNN .
 Law enforcement agencies nationwide use NCIC to share information on warrants and background checks. The latest intrusion was discovered in recent days, as the Trump administration sought to assuage public concern about cybersecurity amid a series of high-profile outages affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the FAA’s air traffic control system.
 Advertisement 
 The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In September, a group called ShinyHunters targeted sensitive personal data of employees through an FBI jobs website. A Canadian cybersecurity researcher and author has been arrested and faces charges related to that breach.
 On Thursday, after bureau officials learned of the latest cybersecurity incident, FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to tout the bureau’s cybersecurity work. He discussed an operation completed months earlier that aimed to urge companies to update their systems and prevent hackers from accessing sensitive data.
 Patel referred to Operation Winter Shield as if it were still underway and praised the current administration for updating key systems to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure.
 “Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said. “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.” 
 - Kash Patel

 FBI Deputy Director Andrew Bailey has resigned, saying he wants to spend more time with his family. His departure raises questions about the bureau’s leadership structure.
